title: Adopter outreach + accepted-source shortlist
context: genome-browser-tracks defines success as delivered, not merged — a track pack that nobody loads is not an outcome. No named lab, educator, browser project, or advocacy org has yet confirmed they will adopt a pack (verifiedNeed is false for all tasks). M0 requires at least one adopter-outreach thread to be opened in parallel with the pilot build, so the adoption blocker is surfaced early and not discovered only after packs are produced.
objective: Open at least one outreach thread with a candidate adopter (academic cancer-genomics lab, bioinformatics course instructor, genome-browser project, or patient-advocacy org), and produce a committed document summarising the outreach status and the accepted-source shortlist for M0/M1 pack selection.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one concrete outreach thread is opened with a named candidate adopter (lab, educator, browser project, or advocacy org) and documented with contact, date, and status.
The outreach document describes the adoption mechanism offered (self-serve hub URL, hub registry listing, lesson integration, or repo reference).
The accepted-source shortlist identifies the M0 pilot source (Open Targets CC0) and candidate M1 sources (CIViC CC0, ClinVar PD) with their license disposition and why they are Priority-A.
Document output licensed CC-BY-4.0; commit is DCO signed-off.
resources: UCSC public hub registry; JBrowse plugin/config registry
output: review/outreach-005-status.md — committed outreach status document and accepted-source shortlist for M0/M1.
